summary: Invite-only user provisioning: admins mint single-use, time-limited invite links, list/revoke them, list users with metadata-only visibility, and delete a user's whole vault — with no decryption, password-reset, or role-change ability anywhere in the surface.

read.role: the only screen this feature drives

tokenEntropy.value: 256 bits, secrets.token_urlsafe(32), shown once at creation, never retrievable afterward

tokenHash.value: SHA-256, looked up by hash, never scanned/compared as plaintext

expiry.value: default 7 days, admin-settable 1-30 days at creation

statusValues.note: expired is derived from expires_at, never stored

sentinelCreatedBy.value: system:bootstrap, refused as a registration username

endpoints.createInvite: POST /api/admin/invites { expiresInDays, label, isAdmin } -> { id, token, url, expiresAt }
endpoints.listInvites: GET /api/admin/invites -> [{ id, label, createdAt, expiresAt, status, usedAt, usedBy }] (never token or hash)
endpoints.revokeInvite: POST /api/admin/invites/<id>/revoke -> status: revoked; idempotent if already revoked, refused (409) if used
endpoints.listUsers: GET /api/admin/users -> [{ username, createdAt, isAdmin, recordCount, lastLoginAt }]
endpoints.deleteUser: DELETE /api/admin/users/<username> { confirmUsername } -> deletes user row, all records, all sessions in one transaction; 400 if confirmUsername mismatches path; 409 if target is the last remaining admin

authRequirement.value: every /api/admin/* endpoint requires an authenticated session with is_admin; a non-admin session gets 404, never 403

noRoleChangeEndpoint.value: no promote/demote endpoint exists anywhere; the only way to make an admin is the bootstrap CLI or an invite created with isAdmin: true

bootstrapCli.value: flask create-invite --admin --expires-days 1; requires --force on a populated instance, printing existing user/admin counts, and does not refuse outright even then

referrerPolicy.value: Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on /register and admin UI pages

tokenUrlScrub.value: the register page removes the token from the address bar via history.replaceState once the form holds it

logRedaction.value: the app strips/redacts the invite token from its own access logging; the deployment's reverse proxy/tunnel logging is documented separately as a place it may still appear

fixtures: a seeded admin session and a seeded non-admin session, for the 404-not-403 assertions across every /api/admin/* route
a bootstrap-CLI-minted invite (created_by: system:bootstrap) alongside an admin-minted one, to test the sentinel username refusal
two populated vaults, for the 'deleting one user leaves the other's records and sessions untouched' criterion
a simulated DB failure mid-delete, for the transactional-rollback criterion
the full response shape of every admin endpoint, for the 'never returns wrapped DEK/salt/KDF envelope/ciphertext' sweep
focus: the 'no endpoint promotes or demotes an admin' criterion requires enumerating every registered route under /api/admin/, not just testing the documented ones

the last-admin guard must be checked on both deletion paths — the admin panel's DELETE /api/admin/users/<username> and the user's own DELETE /api/auth/account (account-settings.md) — a test that only covers one path is incomplete
the invite token must never appear in the application's own log output — requires inspecting actual log lines, not just the HTTP response
the DB-failure-mid-delete criterion needs an actual fault injection (simulated failure) to prove atomicity, not just a happy-path delete test
byte-identical registration errors for invalid/expired/used/revoked invites is a shared assertion with register.md — verify it is asserted once, not divergently in both feature tests
